surprises.head: St. Louis hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: St. Louis’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 49, against their usual 104 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Columbus couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Columbus’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (about 6.4% against St. Louis) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Neighbours sparks a Blues comeback
paras: Valeri Nichushkin scored his first goal for Columbus late in the first to open the scoring, and Kent Johnson made it 2-0 with 12 seconds left in the period. Ross Johnston and Mathieu Olivier opened the second period with a fight. Jake Neighbours scored once and Jimmy Snuggerud twice in less than seven minutes early in the period to turn a 2-0 deficit into a 3-2 lead. Cole Sillinger tied it up for Columbus midway through the third, but that’s where Columbus’ luck ran out. Jonatan Berggren put the Blues ahead for good less than three minutes later, and Pavel Buchnevich added the empty-netter with 43 seconds left to make it 5-3. Dylan Holloway finished with three assists.

The Blues drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. The Blues had four shots in the first period and trailed 2-0, then outshot the Blue Jackets 23-13 the rest of the way. Jordan Binnington made 20 saves for the Blues, and Jet Greaves stopped 22 of 26. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Zach Werenski, even in a loss, by our Swing measure. The Blues improved to 2-2-1, and the Jackets fell to 2-2-0.

items.text: Robert Thomas passed David Backes for tenth on the Blues’ all-time scoring list, with 461 points.
